weeks.title: Python internals and how LLMs actually work
weeks.goal: Fill the gaps interviewers probe first: how Python binds names and runs functions, and what a model does with your tokens. Start the income pipeline on day one.
weeks.deliverable: `llm.py` with streaming and cost logging; Upwork and Fiverr profiles live; two or three platform applications sent.
interview_checks: Why does the same paragraph cost more tokens in Bangla than in English?
What does temperature do to the softmax distribution, and what does top-p do?
What is the difference between `is` and `==`, and when is `is` the right choice?
What does `functools.wraps` preserve, and what breaks without it?
Why is `def f(x=[])` a bug?

lessons.title: Names, objects and mutability
topics: Every value is an object with an identity (`id`), a type and a value
`is` vs `==`; small-integer and string interning
Mutable vs immutable types; assignment binds names, it never copies
The mutable default argument bug and the `None` sentinel fix
Shallow vs deep copy: `copy.copy`, `copy.deepcopy`
lessons.exercise: Write five short snippets that would surprise a junior developer (a list aliased inside a dict, a default-argument list) and explain each in one sentence.

lessons.title: Functions, scope and closures
topics: Functions are first-class: pass them, return them, store them
LEGB scope rule; `global` vs `nonlocal`
Closures and the `__closure__` cells that hold captured variables
The late-binding gotcha with lambdas created in a loop
`*args`, `**kwargs`, keyword-only (`*`) and positional-only (`/`) parameters
lessons.exercise: Build `make_counter()` that returns a function counting how many times it was called, using a closure and `nonlocal`.

lessons.title: Decorators
topics: A decorator takes a callable and returns a callable
`functools.wraps` and why lost metadata breaks logging, FastAPI and tests
Decorators with arguments (three levels of nesting)
Stacking order: the decorator closest to the function runs first
`functools.lru_cache` and `functools.cache`
lessons.exercise: Write `@retry(times=3, backoff=2.0, exceptions=(TimeoutError,))` and `@timed`, then stack both on a fake flaky API call.

lessons.title: Iterators and generators
topics: The iterator protocol: `__iter__`, `__next__`, `StopIteration`
`yield`, generator state, `yield from`
Generator expressions vs list comprehensions, and the memory difference
Lazy pipelines: read → filter → transform
Where this shows up: streaming LLM tokens to a client
lessons.exercise: Stream a large JSONL log file through a generator pipeline and count error lines without loading the file into memory.

lessons.title: Context managers and the data model
topics: `with`, `__enter__` / `__exit__`, and how `__exit__` can suppress exceptions
`contextlib.contextmanager` and `ExitStack`
Dunder methods: `__repr__`, `__eq__`, `__hash__`, `__len__`, `__getitem__`, `__add__`
`@dataclass` options: `frozen`, `slots`, `field(default_factory=...)`
lessons.exercise: Write a `timer()` context manager that logs elapsed milliseconds, and a frozen `Usage` dataclass with `__add__` for summing token counts.

milestones.title: Watch Karpathy’s “Intro to Large Language Models”. Note pretraining, fine-tuning, RLHF, tool use and jailbreaks
Read The Illustrated Transformer: embeddings, self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding
Click through Transformer Explainer and watch attention and the softmax change with temperature
In Tiktokenizer, tokenize the same paragraph in English and in Bangla. Record both counts and the cost ratio
Watch the sampling and hallucination sections of Karpathy’s “Deep Dive into LLMs”
Write a one-page note in your own words: tokens, embeddings, attention, context window, temperature, top-p, why models hallucinate
Work through the API fundamentals lessons: roles, system prompt, `max_tokens`, `stop_reason`, the `usage` fields
Write `llm.py`: one `chat()` function that supports Anthropic and OpenAI and returns text plus a `Usage` dataclass
Add streaming as a generator that yields text deltas
Add a price table per model; log cost per call to JSONL and print totals when the script exits
Open a Payoneer account; verify your NID or passport on Upwork and Fiverr
Apply to Mercor and micro1. Apply to Turing only if 20+ hours a week fits your schedule
Upwork profile: headline “AI Agent & Automation Developer: LLM agents, RAG, n8n, Python”, a results-first overview, and $25–30/hr to start
Create two Fiverr gigs: a RAG chatbot over the client’s documents, and n8n + AI workflow automation
Record a two-minute Loom demo of your best existing LLM project and put it at the top of its README

weeks.title: Production Python and the agent loop from scratch
weeks.goal: Learn the async and typing tools every agent backend uses, then build an agent without a framework so you can explain every step of it in an interview.
weeks.deliverable: `agent-from-scratch` repository: three tools, a guarded loop, JSONL traces, tests and a README.
interview_checks: Walk me through what happens between the model emitting a tool call and receiving the result.
How do you stop an agent from looping forever or burning its budget?
`gather` vs `TaskGroup`: what happens to the other tasks when one fails?
Why validate tool arguments with Pydantic, and what do you do when validation fails?
How do you unit-test code that calls an LLM?

lessons.title: Type hints that matter
topics: `list[int]`, `dict[str, Any]`, `X | None`, `Literal`
`TypedDict` vs `@dataclass` vs a Pydantic model
`Protocol` for structural typing, e.g. an `LLMClient` interface
Generics with `TypeVar`
Run `mypy --strict` or pyright on `llm.py` and fix every error
lessons.exercise: Define a `ToolSpec` TypedDict and an `LLMClient` Protocol; make both of your clients satisfy the Protocol.

lessons.title: Pydantic v2
topics: `BaseModel`, `Field`, defaults and aliases
`field_validator` and `model_validator`
`model_validate`, `model_validate_json`, `model_dump`
`model_json_schema()`: this is how tool input schemas get generated
Catch `ValidationError` and send the message back to the model as feedback
lessons.exercise: Model `GetOrderStatusArgs` and `CreateTicketArgs`, and generate their JSON schemas for tool definitions.

lessons.title: asyncio, part 1
topics: Coroutines vs tasks vs futures
The event loop: `await` hands control back
`asyncio.gather` and `asyncio.create_task`
Why one blocking call (`requests`, `time.sleep`) freezes everything; `asyncio.to_thread`
`async with` and `async for`
lessons.exercise: Call your LLM ten times in sequence, then with `gather`. Time both runs.

lessons.title: asyncio, part 2
topics: `asyncio.Semaphore` to cap concurrency
`asyncio.timeout` and `wait_for`
Cancellation and cleanup: `CancelledError`, `finally`
`TaskGroup` (Python 3.11+) and exception groups
`httpx.AsyncClient` with timeouts and connection pooling
lessons.exercise: Fetch 50 URLs with at most 5 in flight, a 10-second timeout, and 3 retries with exponential backoff.

lessons.title: Testing with pytest
topics: Test discovery, plain `assert`, `pytest -k` and `-x`
Fixtures, fixture scope, `conftest.py`
`@pytest.mark.parametrize`
`monkeypatch` and fake LLM clients: unit tests never call the real API
`pytest-asyncio` for async code
lessons.exercise: Write tests for yesterday’s fetcher and for `llm.py` using a fake client.

milestones.title: Read Anthropic’s tool-use docs and OpenAI’s function-calling guide: tool schemas, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks, `tool_choice`, parallel tool calls
Work through the tool-use lessons in the Anthropic courses repository
Build three tools with Pydantic argument models: `calculator`, `get_order_status` (mock database), `search_docs` (keyword search over a folder of Markdown files)
Rewrite each tool description to say when to use it, what each argument means, and give one example. Read “Writing effective tools for agents” first
The loop: send messages and tools; if the model asks for tools, run every call, append the `tool_result` blocks, and repeat until it answers
Guards: `max_steps`, a per-run cost budget, a timeout per tool, and validation errors returned to the model as text
Trace every step to JSONL: step number, input and output tokens, tool name, arguments, result preview, latency
README: a diagram of the loop, one sample trace, and known failure modes
Send 8 Upwork proposals on AI chatbot, automation and “fix my agent” posts. Open with a two-line diagnosis of their problem
Complete any Mercor or micro1 assessments that have arrived
LinkedIn post: your agent loop and one annotated trace

weeks.title: Coding interview core, structured outputs and context engineering
weeks.goal: Start the data-structures habit (an hour a day is enough) and learn to control what goes into the model and what comes out of it.
weeks.deliverable: Invoice extraction script with validation metrics, and agent v2 with compaction and prompt caching, with a cost table.
interview_checks: When can a structured-output call still give you wrong data?
How does prompt caching work, and what invalidates the cache?
What belongs in the system prompt vs the user turn vs the tool descriptions?
How do you keep a long-running agent inside its context window?
Solve Two Sum in O(n) and explain the hash-map invariant.

lessons.title: Big-O, arrays and hashing (part 1)
topics: Time vs space complexity; amortised cost of `list.append` and dict lookup
Hash maps and sets: when an O(1) lookup is the whole solution
Problems: Contains Duplicate, Valid Anagram, Two Sum, Group Anagrams
lessons.exercise: Say the time and space complexity out loud before you write any code.

lessons.title: Arrays and hashing (part 2)
topics: Bucket-sort idea; prefix and suffix products
Problems: Top K Frequent Elements, Product of Array Except Self, Longest Consecutive Sequence
lessons.exercise: Re-solve Two Sum from memory in under five minutes.

lessons.title: Two pointers
topics: Pointers moving in from both ends of a sorted array
Problems: Valid Palindrome, Two Sum II, 3Sum, Container With Most Water
lessons.exercise: Write the duplicate-skipping logic in 3Sum without looking.

lessons.title: Sliding window
topics: Fixed vs variable window: grow the right edge, shrink the left
Problems: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock, Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters, Longest Repeating Character Replacement
lessons.exercise: Explain why each pointer only moves forward, which makes it O(n).

lessons.title: Stacks
topics: LIFO and the monotonic-stack pattern
Problems: Valid Parentheses, Min Stack, Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation, Daily Temperatures
lessons.exercise: Start a problem log: date, minutes taken, pattern, and the date to redo it.

milestones.title: Compare JSON mode, strict structured outputs and forced tool calls for extraction; note where each can still fail
Anthropic interactive prompt tutorial: chapters on roles, XML tags, few-shot examples, step-by-step thinking and prefill
With Instructor and Pydantic, extract invoices (vendor, date, line items, total) from 10 sample texts; add a validator that checks total = sum of lines
Measure the percentage valid on the first try, and the percentage fixed by one retry that includes the validation error
Read “Effective context engineering for AI agents”
Add context compaction to your agent: once history passes N tokens, summarise old turns and trim long tool results
Add prompt caching to the system prompt and tool definitions; run 20 calls with and without it and record the cost
Put a before/after cost table in the README
Send 8 Upwork proposals on agent, RAG and automation posts. Open with a two-line diagnosis of their problem and a link to your closest project
Send 5 full-time applications on Himalayas, Jobgether or Remote Rocketship with the Bangladesh filter on
LinkedIn post: your Bangla vs English token-cost finding

weeks.title: Backend fundamentals and an agent API
weeks.goal: Put an agent behind a real API with a database, authentication and streaming. Most job posts mean exactly this when they say “production”.
weeks.deliverable: `agent-api`: FastAPI, Postgres, SSE streaming, API-key auth and tests, started with one `docker compose up`.
interview_checks: PUT vs PATCH vs POST: which are idempotent, and why does that matter for retries?
What is inside a JWT, and how would you revoke one?
When does adding an index make things slower?
How do you stream model output to a browser, and what happens when the client disconnects?
What is the N+1 query problem and how do you fix it?

lessons.title: HTTP
topics: Request and response anatomy; methods and idempotency (GET, PUT, PATCH, POST, DELETE)
Headers: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`, `Cache-Control`, `Retry-After`
CORS in one paragraph
lessons.exercise: Run `curl -v` against a public API and label every header you see.

lessons.title: Authentication and authorisation
topics: API keys vs sessions vs JWTs
JWT structure (header.payload.signature) and why revocation is hard
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE (you need it later for MCP)
Password hashing with bcrypt or argon2; secrets never go in git
lessons.exercise: Draw the OAuth authorization code flow from memory.

lessons.title: SQL, part 1
topics: `SELECT`, `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`
`INNER JOIN` vs `LEFT JOIN`
`GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, aggregate functions
Subqueries and CTEs (`WITH`)
lessons.exercise: Finish SQLBolt lessons 1–12, then write five queries against a conversations/messages schema.

lessons.title: SQL, part 2
topics: B-tree indexes; column order in composite indexes
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`
Transactions, ACID, and isolation levels at a high level
The N+1 query problem
lessons.exercise: Add an index to a 100k-row table and compare the `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` output before and after.

lessons.title: Git for teams
topics: Branches, merge vs rebase, resolving conflicts
Partial staging, `--amend`, and `reflog` to recover from mistakes
Good pull requests: small, described, tested; conventional commit messages
lessons.exercise: Complete Learn Git Branching, main levels 1–8.

milestones.title: FastAPI tutorial: path, query and body parameters, Pydantic models, dependencies, error handling
Run Postgres in Docker; model `conversations` and `messages` tables with SQLModel
API-key authentication as a dependency; per-key rate limit with a simple in-memory token bucket
Tests with FastAPI’s `TestClient`
`POST /chat` runs your agent and stores every turn and tool call in Postgres
Stream tokens to the client with server-sent events
Dockerfile and docker-compose (API + Postgres) so one command starts everything
README: API reference and `curl` examples

weeks.title: Agent design patterns: workflows vs agents
weeks.goal: Learn the handful of patterns behind almost every production agent, and when a plain workflow beats an agent.
weeks.deliverable: Patterns repository with five implementations, plus a measured workflow-vs-agent write-up.
interview_checks: Workflow or agent: how do you decide for a given problem?
Explain ReAct. What does the reasoning step buy you?
What goes wrong with orchestrator-workers, and how do you contain it?
Where does evaluator-optimizer waste money?
Implement an LRU cache and say where you would use one in an LLM app.

lessons.title: Binary search
topics: Binary search built on an invariant; getting `lo` and `hi` right
Problems: Binary Search, Search a 2D Matrix, Koko Eating Bananas, Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
lessons.exercise: Write binary search from memory three times with no off-by-one errors.

lessons.title: Linked lists, part 1
topics: Pointer manipulation and the dummy head node
Problems: Reverse Linked List, Merge Two Sorted Lists, Linked List Cycle (Floyd), Reorder List
lessons.exercise: Draw the pointers on paper before coding each problem.

lessons.title: Linked lists, part 2, and the LRU cache
topics: Fast and slow pointers
Problems: Remove Nth Node From End of List, LRU Cache (hash map + doubly linked list)
Why it matters here: LRU is how you cache embeddings or tool results
lessons.exercise: Implement LRU Cache with `OrderedDict`, then again without it.

lessons.title: Trees, part 1
topics: Recursive DFS: pre-order, in-order, post-order
Problems: Invert Binary Tree, Maximum Depth, Diameter of Binary Tree, Balanced Binary Tree, Same Tree
lessons.exercise: Write both a recursive and an iterative DFS for one of the problems.

lessons.title: Trees, part 2
topics: BFS with a queue; level-order traversal
The binary search tree property
Problems: Level Order Traversal, Validate BST, Kth Smallest in a BST, Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
lessons.exercise: Explain the memory use of BFS vs DFS on a wide tree and on a deep tree.
